briefings.title: Chamath: Bitcoin Goes to Zero, Robots vs. $40T Debt, Elon’s SpaceX Shares for 72M Kids | EP #304
briefings.tldr: Chamath Palihapitiya and panelists discuss the arrival of AGI, critical power and compute constraints, and novel economic frameworks—such as Elon Musk's gift of SpaceX stock to 72 million American children and Anthropic's $75B–$100B public benefit fund—while debating the future of fiat currency, national debt, and crypto.

briefings.title: Palmer Luckey: Autonomous Weapons Are Ancient and Why Anduril Won't Build Humanoids | EP #295
briefings.tldr: Palmer Luckey and the panel discussed autonomous defense systems, the realities of AI risk, the rejection of humanoid robots for military use, and the lessons learned from pioneering virtual reality and defense tech.

briefings.title: Google I/O 2026, Karpathy Joins Anthropic, and Cerebras’ $95B IPO | EP #256
briefings.tldr: Google I/O showcased the tech giant’s massive transition into an AI-native operating system powered by an expected $180B–$190B annual CapEx, while Cerebras Systems CEO Andrew Feldman celebrated a historic $95 billion IPO, highlighting a massive market shift toward custom, wafer-scale high-throughput inference chips.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis on AGI, Robots Scale Production, and Elon’s $1T Mars-Shot Comp | EP 253
briefings.tldr: At a special Moonshots panel at MIT, Peter H. Diamandis and exponential technology experts analyzed the rapid scaling of humanoid robotics, the legal battle over OpenAI's corporate governance, and a future where AI-driven scientific discovery and advanced biotechnology reshape global economics and human biology.

briefings.title: Sam Altman’s Attack, Amazon vs. Starlink, and What Opus 4.7 Actually Means | #248
briefings.tldr: Anthropic's Opus 4.7 dropped to mixed reviews amid rising AI anxiety and physical backlash, while the Stanford 2026 AI Index highlighted soaring benchmarks alongside youth hiring freezes and falling model transparency.

briefings.title: Elon Musk vs. Sam Altman, AI Job Loss, and OpenAI’s $852B Valuation | EP #247
briefings.tldr: The AI industry is entering a "geopolitical and governance war" phase, characterized by the Musk vs. Altman $100B lawsuit, massive capital redirection toward Anthropic, and the rapid migration of AI intelligence into physical robotics and biological drug discovery.

briefings.title: Eric Schmidt: Singularity's Arrival, 92-Gigawatt Problem & Recursive Self-Improvement Timeline | 241
briefings.tldr: The world is approaching a "superintelligence moment" within two to three years driven by recursive self-improvement and AI agents, but this progression faces a critical 92-gigawatt power shortage and intense competition from China’s vertically integrated robotics industry.

briefings.title: Elon Musk: Optimus 3 Is Coming, Recursive Self-Improvement Is Already Here, and the Singularity #239
briefings.tldr: Elon Musk predicts a "hard takeoff" for AI with full recursive self-improvement by 2025, leading to a 10x expansion of the global economy within a decade and an eventual post-scarcity era of "Universal High Income."

briefings.title: AI CEOs Come Online: Sam Altman's Replacement Plan, Job Loss & 'Solve Everything' Launches | EP #230
briefings.tldr: As AI transitions from a tool to a governance actor, the global economy is shifting from a "war on ignorance" to a "war on scarcity," necessitating a transition from paying for labor inputs to paying for verified, industrial-scale outcomes.
